resources.string: Transport: your local Wi-Fi network (TCP, AES-GCM encrypted). Bluetooth is not used for audio. Both phones must be on the same Wi-Fi network or hotspot.
Audio from apps or content that block capture (for example DRM-protected streams) cannot be shared. Android decides this, not NearAudio. Your own phone keeps playing the audio too.
Sharing needs the microphone permission only because Android requires it for playback capture. NearAudio never records the microphone, saves no audio and sends nothing to the internet.
No phones found yet. Start discovery on both phones and check that they are on the same Wi-Fi network (some guest networks block device-to-device traffic).
Start discovery to find nearby phones running NearAudio.
At most %d recipients at a time.

%1$s wants to play its audio on your phone.

Verification code: %2$s

Only accept if the same code is shown on their phone.
No sound captured for several seconds. Either nothing is playing, or the app you are playing from blocks audio capture.
Permission denied. Android requires the microphone permission to capture playback audio. Enable it in system settings for NearAudio.
Screen/audio capture consent was not given, so nothing is shared.
Discovery problem (code %s). Is Wi-Fi turned on?
Could not open a network port: %s
Connect to at least one phone before sharing.
Stop listening before connecting to other phones.
Sharing audio with %d phone(s) over local Wi-Fi
Step 1: start discovery so nearby phones can be found.
Step 2: select phones below and tap Connect.
Step 3: tap Start sharing audio, then play something in another app.
Tap Start listening and keep this screen open.
Keep this screen open. The sharing phone will connect and you confirm the code.
Transport: Bluetooth LE, no Wi-Fi or internet needed (AES-GCM encrypted). Audio is compressed to fit Bluetooth, so quality is lower than over Wi-Fi; range and stability depend on your phones.
Low delay may stutter on a weak connection. Stable adds a little delay but avoids dropouts.
Step 2: select phones below and tap Connect. Bluetooth must be on for both phones.
Keep this screen open and Bluetooth on. The sharing phone finds you; confirm the code.
No phones found yet. The other phone must choose Listen + Bluetooth and become visible.
Bluetooth problem (%s). Is Bluetooth on and permission granted?
Bluetooth mode needs the nearby-devices permission (location on Android 11 and older).
Bluetooth mode asks for nearby-devices permission (Android 12+) or location (Android 11 and older, required by Android for Bluetooth scanning). NearAudio never reads your location.
Bluetooth earbuds are connected to this phone. They share the radio with this link and can cause dropouts. Use Max buffer, or use Wi-Fi or Wired mode instead.
Playing audio from the wired input
USB cable connected – waiting for the sharing phone
USB cable connected – select it below and tap Connect

Transport: USB cable between the phones (Android Open Accessory, full quality, no radio, AES-GCM encrypted). The sharing phone must be the USB host: plug the OTG adapter or the cable end that powers the link into the SHARING phone. Accept the USB permission prompts on both phones.

Transport: analog cable. Connect the sharing phone\'s headphone output (or USB audio adapter) to the audio input of this phone (headset jack or USB audio adapter). Quality is limited by the cable and input.
Connect the USB cable (OTG adapter on this phone), then tap Search USB device and accept the prompts.
Connect the USB cable, tap Wait for USB cable and accept the prompt. Then confirm the code when the sharing phone connects.
Nothing to do in the app: plug the cable into this phone\'s headphone output (or USB audio adapter), set a high volume and play audio normally. The other phone chooses Listen + Wired + Audio input.
Connect the cable to this phone\'s headset/USB audio input and tap the button. The audio plays on your earbuds or speaker.
No USB phone linked yet. Check the cable and the OTG adapter, and that the other phone chose Listen + Wired + USB cable.
USB problem (%s). Check the cable, OTG adapter and accept the permission prompts.
No usable wired audio input found (%s). Connect the cable first (headset jack or USB audio adapter with input).
Playing audio from the wired input
